target.title: feat: add Twilio RCS channel [AI]
target.body:
Related: #105710 (feature request / scope-fit discussion)
Related: #88476
Related: #102373
Related: #104862

## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw can send and receive SMS through Twilio today, but SMS cannot carry most of the conversational surfaces OpenClaw is built around: no delivery/read receipts, no rich media or suggested actions, 160-character segment fragmentation, and an anonymous 10-digit sender identity. RCS restores those capabilities on a plain phone number, and core is already meeting real RCS traffic — #102373 (merged) had to teach the SMS channel to normalize Twilio `rcs:` addresses because Twilio Messaging Services with RCS senders are live in the field today. What is missing is a first-class channel: `rcs:+E164` targets, RCS webhooks, delivery/**read** status capture, pairing/allowlist access control, and safe coexistence with existing SMS webhook setups.

## Why This Change Was Made

This adds an `rcs` channel plugin modeled on the existing SMS channel (#88476) while keeping RCS-specific behavior separate: RCS address normalization, outbound send handling, inbound webhook dispatch, status callback capture (including post-delivery `EventType=READ` read receipts), channel config metadata, plugin inventory/docs, and generated channel-config discovery are all included.

Beyond feature parity with the SMS channel's architecture, the channel carries the value that justifies it:

- **Read receipts and delivery states** — outbound status progresses through `sent`/`delivered`/`read`, so an agent can know a message was seen instead of guessing from silence.
- **Rich media and structured actions** — full-resolution media and inbound button-tap payloads (`ButtonText`/`ButtonPayload`) the agent can route on.
- **Verified sender identity** — an RCS sender is a carrier- and platform-vetted agent with a branded profile page (name, logo, description, contact details) instead of an anonymous number. For business and compliance-sensitive deployments this is a meaningful anti-spoofing/anti-phishing property, and the registration/vetting behind it is what compliance reviews typically ask for.

Provider posture mirrors the SMS channel: Twilio RCS Business Messaging is the initial supported provider, Twilio-specific webhook/API handling is isolated in the provider layer, and the channel surface itself (`rcs` id, `rcs:+E164` addressing, pairing policy, status capture) stays provider-neutral so additional RBM providers can back the same channel.

Hardening goes where the SMS channel has already been: the shared SMS/RCS Twilio webhook path is guarded so one public route cannot loop or fight with the dedicated RCS route; the coarse rate limiter mirrors the SMS no-silent-drop behavior from #104862 by acknowledging signature-validated over-limit Twilio callbacks instead of returning a non-2xx that Twilio treats as delivery failure; the loopback SMS forward uses the SDK's guarded local-origin fetch rather than raw `fetch()`; and outbound text passes through `sanitizeAssistantVisibleText`.

## User Impact

Users and operators can configure a Twilio RCS sender as an OpenClaw channel, send to RCS phone-number targets, receive inbound RCS messages (including button taps), and collect RCS delivery/read receipts. Private deployments can use pairing or allowlists, while shared SMS/RCS Twilio webhook deployments get documented setup constraints and startup warnings for unsafe route combinations. Docs cover the RBM test-phase notice and launch expectations so operators are not surprised by client-side test banners.

This PR is AI-assisted.

## Evidence

Focused local validation on current `upstream/main` head `23251474df0eb8ba27b70eba89a51c79e1e9d34e`:

- `git diff --check`
- `PNPM_CONFIG_VERIFY_DEPS_BEFORE_RUN=false corepack pnpm config:channels:check`
- `PNPM_CONFIG_VERIFY_DEPS_BEFORE_RUN=false corepack pnpm plugins:inventory:check`
- `PNPM_CONFIG_VERIFY_DEPS_BEFORE_RUN=false corepack pnpm docs:map:check`
- `PNPM_CONFIG_VERIFY_DEPS_BEFORE_RUN=false OPENCLAW_VITEST_MAX_WORKERS=1 corepack pnpm test extensions/rcs` — 5 files, 56 tests passed
- `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.extensions.test.json` (noUncheckedIndexedAccess lane) — clean
- `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p extensions/rcs/tsconfig.json` — clean
- `node scripts/check-no-raw-channel-fetch.mjs` — clean
- `vitest run src/plugins/contracts/extension-package-project-boundaries.test.ts` — 8 passed
- `vitest run src/channels/plugins/contracts/plugin.registry-backed-shard-h.contract.test.ts` — 3 passed (bundled public surface `rcs/channel-plugin-api.js` resolves)
- `OPENCLAW_OXLINT_SKIP_LOCK=1 OPENCLAW_OXLINT_SKIP_PREPARE=1 timeout 180 node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.extensions.json extensions/rcs`

The heavier repo-wide lanes (full `tsgo:all`, full lint, import-cycle checks, shrinkwrap regeneration) were intentionally left to GitHub-hosted CI, which remains canonical for those gates.

Not live-tested against a production Twilio RCS sender in this PR branch; provider behavior is covered by focused Twilio signature/payload/unit tests (including `EventType=READ` read-receipt mapping verified against Twilio's status-callback documentation) and docs, with live configuration expected to be operator-specific.
